annotation.title_clean: UN Regulation No 155 – Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regards to cybersecurity and cybersecurity management system
annotation.title_en: UN Regulation No 155 – Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regards to cybersecurity and cybersecurity management system
annotation.authors_or_issuer: UN/ECE World Forum for Harmonization of Vehicle Regulations (WP.29); published in the Official Journal of the European Union
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, L 82/30
annotation.summary_en: UN Regulation No 155 sets uniform requirements for type approval of road vehicles regarding cybersecurity. Manufacturers must hold a certified Cybersecurity Management System covering development, production and post-production, perform risk assessments against listed threats, implement mitigations, monitor and report annually. Applies to M, N, O categories and L vehicles with level 3+ automated driving.
key_provisions_or_claims: Applies to categories M and N, O with ECUs, and L with automated driving level 3 or higher
Manufacturers need a Certificate of Compliance for CSMS, valid maximum three years
Mandatory risk assessment against Annex 5 threats with proportionate mitigations and pre-approval testing
Continual monitoring, attack detection, forensic logging and at least annual reporting to approval authority
Type approval can be refused or withdrawn for non-compliance; authorities share assessment methods via UNECE DETA database
